record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Bregman analogues of Chebyshev and Klee functions
record.original_question: Let X = R^n and let g: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a proper lower semicontinuous function. In the Euclidean theory of Chebyshev and Klee functions, the discrepancy is q(x) = (1/2)||x||^2, the halved Euclidean distance squared. What are the corresponding characterizations when that Euclidean discrepancy is replaced by a Bregman distance generated by a Legendre function f? In particular, how should one characterize the admissible generator f and the associated Chebyshev point in the Bregman-distance setting?

evidence.quote: Chebyshev set and Klee set problems can be generalized to problems involving functions. Throughout this section, g : X -> [-infinity, +infinity] is lower semicontinuous and proper.
For convenience, we also set q := 1/2 ||.||^2.
Problem 7. For the Chebyshev functions and Klee functions, we have used the halved Euclidean distance. What are characterizations of f and Chebyshev point of f when one uses the Bregman distances?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $g:X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper lower semicontinuous function. In the Euclidean setting, define the halved squared-distance discrepancy $q(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}\|x\|^2$, and recall that:
- the Chebyshev (proximal) function of $g$ is $\mathrm{env}_g(x)=\inf_{y\in X}\{g(y)+q(x-y)\}$, and $g$ is called a Chebyshev function if the proximal mapping $\mathrm{Prox}_g(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y}\{g(y)+q(x-y)\}$ is single-valued for every $x\in X$;
- the Klee (farthest) function of $g$ is $\sup_{y\in X}\{q(x-y)-g(y)\}$, and $g$ is called a Klee function if the farthest mapping is single-valued for every $x\in X$.

Now replace $q$ by a Bregman distance. Let $f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a Legendre function (i.e., a proper lower semicontinuous convex function that is essentially smooth and essentially strictly convex on $\mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{dom}\,f$), and define the Bregman distance
$$D_f(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\langle \nabla f(y),\,x-y\rangle,\qquad x\in\mathrm{dom}\,f,\ y\in\mathrm{int}\,\mathrm{dom}\,f.$$
Replace $q(x-y)$ by $D_f(x,y)$ (or by $D_f(y,x)$ for the right Bregman variant) in the definitions of the proximal and farthest envelopes of $g$.

Problem: Provide intrinsic characterizations, in the Bregman-distance setting, of:
(i) the class of Legendre generators $f$ for which the Bregman Chebyshev (respectively Klee) function of $g$ is well-defined and has the expected single-valuedness and regularity properties;
(ii) the Bregman Chebyshev point (the unique minimizer in the Bregman proximal problem) of a proper lsc function $g$ in terms of $f$, $g$, and the geometry induced by $D_f$.

That is, determine necessary and sufficient conditions on $f$ and on $g$ under which $g$ is a Bregman-Chebyshev (resp. Bregman-Klee) function, and give an explicit description of the associated Chebyshev point.
artifact.status_search_result: Related work has established Bregman analogues of Klee sets and Chebyshev centers (e.g., uniqueness of Klee sets and Chebyshev centers with respect to right Bregman distances induced by Legendre functions), and Chebyshev/Klee functions have been studied in the Euclidean case. However, a complete characterization of admissible Legendre generators $f$ and of the Bregman Chebyshev point at the level of functions (rather than sets) does not appear to be definitively settled in the literature surveyed; partial results exist but a full answer to the stated problem remains unverified.

status_evidence.title: Klee sets and Chebyshev centers for the right Bregman distance
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness of Klee sets and Chebyshev centers proven for right Bregman distances induced by Legendre functions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial Bregman analogues exist at the set level.

status_evidence.title: On Chebyshev functions and Klee functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Chebyshev and Klee functions in the Euclidean (halved squared norm) setting.
status_evidence.claim: Function-level Chebyshev/Klee theory exists in the Euclidean case.

status_evidence.title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems including extension of Chebyshev/Klee function characterizations to Bregman distances.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is posed as an open question in this survey.
